subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Left-sided transient ischemic symptoms.

subs.title: Findings
items: Adequate temporal windows.
Right MCA demonstrates normal spectral waveforms and MFV of 55 cm/s.

Left MCA (depth 50 mm) demonstrates focal acceleration of peak systolic velocity (PSV 185 cm/s, MFV 115 cm/s, normal PI) with high-frequency turbulence, musical bruits, and post-stenotic flow disturbance.
ACA, PCA, and vertebrobasilar systems are unremarkable.

subs.title: Impression
items: High-grade stenosis of the left middle cerebral artery (M1 segment), evidenced by focal velocity acceleration and turbulence. Correlate with MRA/CTA.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Day 5 post-SAH, monitoring for vasospasm.

subs.title: Findings
items: Serial daily comparison shows interval marked acceleration across bilateral middle cerebral arteries.
Right MCA MFV: 145 cm/s (Lindegaard ratio: 3.4).
Left MCA MFV: 155 cm/s (Lindegaard ratio: 3.6).
Bilateral anterior and posterior cerebral arteries show moderately elevated velocities.

subs.title: Impression
items: Moderate-to-severe bilateral middle cerebral artery vasospasm. Elevated Lindegaard ratios (> 3.0) indicate significant vasospasm rather than hyperperfusion. Immediate clinical correlation advised.

bank.title: 4. Intracranial Raised ICP / Elevated Resistance Index

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Altered mental status, suspicion of elevated intracranial pressure.

subs.title: Findings
items: Insonation of bilateral middle cerebral arteries demonstrates markedly high-resistance spectral waveforms globally.
Elevated Pulsatility Indices (PI > 1.4 bilaterally) characterized by sharp systolic peaks, reduced diastolic flow velocities, and near-zero or minimal end-diastolic flow.
No evidence of flow arrest.

subs.title: Impression
items: Diffuse high-resistance intracranial arterial flow pattern, raising suspicion for elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) / decreased cerebral perfusion pressure. Clinical correlation mandatory.

bank.title: 5. Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO) / Right-to-Left Shunt Detection (Bubble Study TCD)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Evaluation for embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS).

subs.title: Findings
items: Baseline monitoring of the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) via temporal window established.
Agitated saline contrast administered via peripheral IV line at rest and followed by Valsalva maneuver at 10 and 30 seconds.
At rest: 0 microembolic signals (MES) detected.
Post-Valsalva release: A shower (> 30 microembolic signals / "curtain effect") of high-intensity transient signals (HITS) detected within 5 seconds in the right MCA spectrum.

subs.title: Impression
items: Positive transcranial Doppler microemboli detection study for right-to-left shunt (Grade IV / massive shunt), highly suggestive of Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO).
